thread.title: Union City man convicted in point-blank shooting of Mountain View officer - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Union City man convicted in point-blank shooting of Mountain View officer - NewsBreak

author: Aldo Toledo
title: Union City man convicted in point-blank shooting of Mountain View officer - NewsBreak
text:
By Aldo Toledo ,
5 hours ago Jeffrey Choy, 37, is seen pointing a gun at a Mountain View police officer before shooting him in an image taken from the officer’s body-worn camera. A jury convicted Choy this week for the 2022 shooting. (Mountain View Police Department) A Santa Clara County jury has convicted a man who shot a police officer at point-blank range during a traffic stop in 2022, prosecutors said Wednesday.
Jeffrey Choy, 37, of Union City, was found guilty of attempted murder for the July 16, 2022 shooting, according to the Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office.
The officer, who has since recovered and is back on duty, had been conducting DUI enforcement downtown. He stopped the driver of a Ford Explorer around midnight after witnessing him blowing through a stop sign at the intersection of Villa and Hope streets.
As the officer approached Choy’s window, the two greeted each other. Choy then pulled out a 9mm handgun and fired two shots at the officer. One round missed, police said, while the other passed through the officer’s arm before striking his bulletproof vest. The shots were fired from “an arm’s length away,” according to authorities.
Choy sped off but later crashed near Higdon Avenue and fled on foot. After hiding in a laundry room for hours, Choy eventually escaped Mountain View. He was arrested the next day outside a Black Bear Diner in Fremont, where he was having brunch with his family, prosecutors said.
At the time of the shooting, Choy was a felon and was not allowed to carry any weapons. He was also out on bail and had an active warrant for possessing a gun during a March 2022 traffic stop.
Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen praised the jury for its decision.
“This verdict reminds us that every time a law enforcement officer starts their shift, they are risking their lives to protect us and our families,” Rosen said. “I thank this officer and every officer who has made it their professional responsibility to put themselves between our community and extremely dangerous people.”
Choy faces life in prison. His sentencing hearing has not been scheduled.
